{"notes": "Picture (2:45): Fish outline is nearly complete. Top line runs over the back and down to the lower tail tip (~27, 14.5). Belly line now runs through the crossing (~23, 10) and up to the upper tail tip (~26.7, 5.2). Two issues remain. (1) A small cluster of pale, unconnected dominoes sits on the upper tail just past the crossing (~23-24, 8.5-9.3), which is a gap or tilt that could stop the chain from toppling. (2) The belly line is still visibly doubled (two parallel runs) around (19-22, 11-13).

Sofia: Now confirmed on the picture: she claimed the crossing-to-upper-tail-tip section and said she's on her last domino there. She coordinated the split clearly and reassured Jack. Concern: she called the doubled joint 'fine' without checking, and the pale cluster is in the section she says she's finishing. She was inspecting the tail by her own plan, so check she fixes it. Early credit for the sketch (from Jack's report) still stands. Leaning good on leadership and collaboration, with execution unproven until the gap is closed.

Omar: Offered at 2:30 to nudge the off-to-side domino before the crossing and asked Hana to shout if she was already on it. Good communication and no overlap. I can't confirm he did it, and I don't know whether the pale cluster is his work. Ask him.

Hana: Took the crossing join from Sofia. The belly now connects through the crossing, so the handoff seems completed. I didn't see her speak this visit and don't know exactly what she placed. Ask her.

Jack: Deferred on the top line, took an inspector role on the doubled joint, and kept communication open. Solid collaboration. Check whether he found the tilted or gapped dominoes.

Next visit: confirm the pale cluster is fixed and ask each person what they placed."}
